summary: Live Oak lookout near Crestview: Florida Forest Service tower built 1953, retired 1983, bought by the city about 2005, now beside its environmental center; NHLR 1000.

access.note: Stands beside the city's McMahon Environmental Center on Butler Circle. No source read says the tower can be climbed.

visit.trail_note: Center is on Butler Circle, off Mapoles Street (City of Crestview).

events.note: Constructed by the Florida Forest Service; named for a nearby cemetery
Operated about 30 years, then put on standby and retired in 1983 (NHLR)
City bought the land, two buildings, a warehouse and the tower from the state for $67,000. Year inferred: the January 7, 2006 article says the purchase was one year earlier
NHLR date registered March 14, 2014; the register lists it as its 1000th fire lookout

evidence.supports: Built 1953 by the Florida Forest Service, named for a nearby cemetery
evidence.quote: When the Florida Forest Service constructed the Live Oak tower in 1953, named for a nearby cemetery

evidence.supports: One of the last links to full fire detection coverage in west Florida
evidence.quote: it was one of the last links to achieve full fire detection coverage for west Florida.

evidence.supports: About 30 years in operation, then standby and retirement in 1983
evidence.quote: Operated for 30 years, it was put on standby service and eventually retired in 1983

evidence.supports: Land around the tower changed from forests to farms and housing
evidence.quote: as the land around it changed from forests to farms and housing

evidence.supports: City acquired the tower and forestry buildings for an environmental center
evidence.quote: the City of Crestview acquired the tower and the forestry buildings for use as an Environmental Center

evidence.supports: Register calls the site a loved landmark
Listed as the 1000th fire lookout on the register
evidence.quote: It has the singular honor of being the 1000th fire lookout to be listed on the National Register.

evidence.supports: City paid the state $67,000 for five acres, two buildings, a warehouse and the tower
evidence.quote: The city paid the state $67,000 for a total of five acres, two buildings, a warehouse space and the old fire tower that stretches high above the treetops of even the tallest, oldest trees in the park.

evidence.supports: Purchase happened one year before the January 2006 article
evidence.quote: This past winter one year ago, the city purchased the land from the state.

evidence.supports: Park is under the city's Division of Leisure Services
evidence.quote: The park is now under the city's umbrella of the Division of Leisure Services.

evidence.supports: Environmental Center is on Butler Circle off Mapoles Street, right next to the fire tower
evidence.quote: The Environmental Center is located on Butler Circle (off of Mapoles Street), right next to the fire tower in Crestview.

evidence.supports: Park was acquired from the Florida Division of Forestry
evidence.quote: was acquired from the Florida Division of Forestry.

evidence.supports: Several hundred children visit each school year
evidence.quote: Several hundred children visit this park each school year.

evidence.supports: January 2015 item says the tower now bears registration number 1,000
evidence.quote: The Liveoak Lookout Tower at the McMahon Environmental Center in Crestview now bears the registration number 1,000 on the National Historic Lookout Register.

evidence.supports: The January 2006 item is a Crestview News Bulletin report

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives March 14, 2014 as the registration date. The News Bulletin item reporting that the tower now bears number 1,000 is dated January 26, 2015. These are not in conflict: the newspaper reported the number a year after registration.

sources.title: Liveoak Fire Lookout becomes nationally recognized

notes_for_editor: The 2005 purchase year is inferred from a January 7, 2006 article saying one year ago, and it is shown as inferred. The News Bulletin 2015 article is paywalled after its first paragraph, so only the registration sentence was used. No design or height is given in the sources read. No dated source confirms the tower's current condition beyond the undated city page calling it the fire tower beside the center. Climbing access is undocumented.
